defects: Reference/junior reuse server ids for created rows, so repeated practice ids can cause several rows to be edited/deleted together; senior already gives created rows UUIDs.
Reference/junior omit HTTP checks and all three lack usable load/create failure branches.
All three clear the field after awaiting a create, overwriting text typed during the request; pending duplicate submission is not handled.
Original seven-row/single-create checks accept reused server ids and a seven-post cap.
rationale: Preserve reference promise chain, junior explicit loops and senior fetchJson/PostItem/useCallback styles. Create only after success, keep a stable client UUID with serverId separate, preserve submitted trimmed text and reject blank/pending submits. Clear the submitted draft at start; a failure restores it only into an empty field and leaves posts/local edits untouched. Add separate fatal load error and recoverable create error, with checked HTTP/JSON/network and request ownership for initial GET. A12post/three-create model edits/deletes just one of repeated server ids; pending/failure/newer-typing, empty/parent/separate/fresh cases hold declared new policies. Old four waits are bounded to300ms so incomplete answers report failures inside the shared suite budget. The comparison strips UI-button text and separator-edge whitespace; it is finite rendering evidence, not proof over arbitrary formatting.
